doc.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022

title: How Sheller starts an original piece
summary: He begins with a rhythm and bass line that imply chords, melody comes later; ideas jotted by his bed after listening to albums.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Can you tell me, I was going to ask this later but I’m going to go for it now. If you’re in the mood to write something original, or you get a request or a commission for something brand new, is there a way that you get started on that?
Yes. It’ll be either thinking of what rhythm I want to use and then a bass line that implies some chords, and we go from there.
I’m smiling because I have to have a bass line myself.

Yep. It’s interesting how, starting from scratch that bass line indicates certain chords, or, it’s funny that the melody usually comes a little further down the line. The rhythm and the bass line come first.
Are you sitting in front of the keyboard when you do that?
And I wonder, if you’re anything like me, do musical — once you get started do musical ideas to add to it come into your head when you’re away from the keyboard?

Yes. I have a piece of manuscript paper at the side of my bed for those moments where I’ll just — usually it comes from my listening to an album, someone’s album that I’m interested in, and somewhere during the course of that I’ll say to myself, “Gee that’s kind of nice, I think I’d like to write something in that groove.”
And you have the ability to write down what you’re hearing in your head fairly accurately?
Fairly accurately, yes. That’s sort of like the basis. Once I get to the keyboard I embellish on that, and that’s how different chords and different voicings come into play.
